annotation.title_clean: Is It Time to Consider EU Criminal Law Rules on Robotics?
annotation.title_en: Is It Time to Consider EU Criminal Law Rules on Robotics?
annotation.venue: Croatian Yearbook of European Law and Policy
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Journal article arguing the EU should develop criminal law rules on AI and robots. It maps areas where AI aids prosecution and where AI acts as 'perpetrator' (autonomous vehicles, surgical robots, autonomous weapons, trading agents), and proposes amending TFEU Article 83 and adopting a directive on abstract-danger offences, corporate liability and command responsibility.
key_provisions_or_claims: Criminal law has been disregarded in EU AI regulation so far, despite civil law initiatives and ethics guidelines.
TFEU Article 83(1) should be expanded to include 'criminal offences connected to autonomous intelligence'.
A directive should create abstract-danger offences in the special part of criminal codes and require corporate criminal liability.
Command responsibility rules should be reconsidered for autonomous weapons.
Common EU standards are needed on admissibility of AI-generated evidence and AI use in criminal proceedings.
